[strategy/guidance/security/Data/GUID-SEC-DATA-REF-1.5.01.md#abb-context]

### ABB Context

- **Parent Vision**: [GUID-SEC-DATA-VISION-0.5.01 — Data Security Architecture Vision](GUID-SEC-DATA-VISION-0.5.01.md)
- **ABB Type**: Composite — this ABB defines the structural composition of the Data Security domain. It is not an implementation specification. It defines boundaries, decomposition, and inter-ABB relationships.
- **Capability Statement**: Defines the complete architectural decomposition of the Data Security domain into component ABBs — establishing how the domain is structured, how component ABBs relate to each other, and what each component is responsible for within the domain.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/security/Data/GUID-SEC-DATA-REF-1.5.01.md#composite-abb-scope]

### Composite ABB Scope

**In Scope**:
- Domain decomposition — identifying the component ABB boundaries within the Data Security domain
- Inter-ABB interface definitions — establishing which component ABBs produce and consume architectural outputs from other component ABBs within the domain
- Domain boundary definition — establishing what is in scope for the Data Security domain versus adjacent domains
- Structural constraints — establishing architectural rules that apply across all component ABBs in the domain

**Out of Scope**:
- Implementation specifications for any individual capability — those belong in Component ABBs and their paired Reference Architecture Documents (RADs)
- Security controls, configuration baselines, and compliance mandates (belong in `standards/security/`)
- Vendor or product selections

### Structural Model

The Data Security domain is decomposed into ten Component ABBs, organized into three functional groups:

**Group 1 — Data Context and Governance (Foundational)**

These ABBs establish the context that all other Data Security capabilities consume. They must be architecturally mature before the protective ABBs in Group 2 can be effectively applied.

| Component ABB | GUID | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Data Classification and Cataloging | [GUID-SEC-DATA-CLASSIFY-2.5.02](GUID-SEC-DATA-CLASSIFY-2.5.02.md) | Draft |
| Data Access Governance | GUID-SEC-DATA-ACCESS-GOV-2.5.07 | Planned |
| Data Privacy and Residency | GUID-SEC-DATA-PRIVACY-2.5.08 | Planned |

**Group 2 — Data Protection Controls (Protective)**

These ABBs apply cryptographic, preventive, and obfuscation protections to data — they consume classification context from Group 1.

| Component ABB | GUID | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Encryption | [GUID-SEC-DATA-ENC-2.5.03](GUID-SEC-DATA-ENC-2.5.03.md) | Draft |
| Key and Secrets Management | [GUID-SEC-DATA-KMS-2.5.04](GUID-SEC-DATA-KMS-2.5.04.md) | Draft |
| Data Loss Prevention | [GUID-SEC-DATA-DLP-2.5.05](GUID-SEC-DATA-DLP-2.5.05.md) | Draft |
| Data Masking and Tokenization | [GUID-SEC-DATA-MASK-2.5.06](GUID-SEC-DATA-MASK-2.5.06.md) | Draft |
| Post-Quantum Cryptography | [GUID-SEC-DATA-PQ-CRYPTO-2.5.01](GUID-SEC-DATA-PQ-CRYPTO-2.5.01.md) | Draft |

**Group 3 — Data Lifecycle and Integrity (Sustaining)**

These ABBs govern how data is managed and verified over time — they apply across the full data lifecycle.

| Component ABB | GUID | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Secure Data Lifecycle Management | GUID-SEC-DATA-LIFECYCLE-2.5.09 | Planned |
| Data Integrity and Non-Repudiation | GUID-SEC-DATA-INTEGRITY-2.5.10 | Planned |

[strategy/guidance/security/Data/GUID-SEC-DATA-REF-1.5.01.md#primary-inter-abb-dependencies]

### Primary Inter-ABB Dependencies

The following dependency chain defines the structural backbone of the Data Security domain:

```text
GUID-SEC-DATA-CLASSIFY-2.5.02 (Classification)
    -- feeds --> GUID-SEC-DATA-ENC-2.5.03 (Encryption tier selection)
    -- feeds --> GUID-SEC-DATA-DLP-2.5.05 (Policy enforcement context)
    -- feeds --> GUID-SEC-DATA-MASK-2.5.06 (Masking requirements)
    -- feeds --> GUID-SEC-DATA-ACCESS-GOV-2.5.07 (Access policy context)

GUID-SEC-DATA-ENC-2.5.03 (Encryption)
    -- consumes --> GUID-SEC-DATA-KMS-2.5.04 (Key material)

GUID-SEC-DATA-KMS-2.5.04 (Key and Secrets Management)
    -- accepts migration path from --> GUID-SEC-DATA-PQ-CRYPTO-2.5.01 (Quantum-resistant key types)
```
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/Data/GUID-SEC-DATA-REF-1.5.01.md#domain-boundary-constraints]

### Domain Boundary Constraints

The following architectural constraints apply across all Component ABBs in this domain:

1. **No security controls in ABBs** — Security controls, configuration requirements, and compliance mandates belong in `standards/security/`. Component ABBs define architectural intent and structural requirements only.

2. **No vendor or product names** — Component ABBs and RADs are vendor-agnostic. Solution-specific implementations are documented as Solution Building Blocks (SBBs) in `realized_by_sbbs`.

3. **Classification is foundational** — No protective Component ABB in Group 2 SHALL define its own classification logic. All protective ABBs consume classification context from GUID-SEC-DATA-CLASSIFY-2.5.02.

4. **Key material governance is centralized** — All ABBs that use cryptographic operations consume key material through the governance framework defined in GUID-SEC-DATA-KMS-2.5.04. ABBs SHALL NOT define independent key management.

5. **Paired RADs are illustrative** — Reference Architecture Documents paired with Component ABBs illustrate implementation approaches. They are non-prescriptive and do not override the architectural intent of this Composite ABB.

[strategy/guidance/security/Data/GUID-SEC-DATA-REF-1.5.01.md#zero-trust-alignment-nist-sp-800-207]

## Zero Trust Alignment (NIST SP 800-207)

This Composite ABB spans the Data pillar of the Zero Trust Architecture. Collectively, the Component ABBs in this domain ensure that data assets carry their own classification-driven protection regardless of the network, system, or user context in which they reside — enabling the Zero Trust principle that protection must be intrinsic to the data, not dependent on perimeter trust.
